name: CrewAI
summary: Python framework for orchestrating role-based autonomous agents, combining Crews (agent teams with task delegation) and Flows (event-driven, state-managed workflows). A separate commercial product, CrewAI AMP, adds managed deployment, a trace dashboard, and webhook automations.

agent-runtime.note: Agents execute a tool-calling loop over assigned tasks within a Crew, with configurable retry limits and execution hooks.

orchestration.note: Flows provide event-driven workflows with state persistence and conditional branching; Crews provide multi-agent task delegation.

knowledge-memory.note: A unified Memory class backed by LanceDB plus Knowledge sources (text, PDF, CSV, Excel, JSON) embedded into ChromaDB or Qdrant with query-rewritten search.

tools-integration.note: Tool calling with a built-in tool library and native MCP server support over stdio, SSE, and streamable HTTP.

identity-governance.note: Task guardrails (function-based and model-based) and human-in-the-loop input are built in, but the framework has no multi-tenant IAM, quota, or audit-log layer.

observability.note: Built-in tracing captures execution time, token usage, and cost, but traces are viewed in the commercial CrewAI AMP dashboard.

data-secrets.note: No managed file storage or encrypted secrets store; credentials are supplied through environment variables.

evaluation.note: The crewai test command scores crew runs across iterations, but it is OpenAI-only and has no dataset or reusable scorer abstraction.

channels.note: Channels run a Crew or Flow as a Slack or Discord bot, but the adapters are third-party CopilotKit packages rather than CrewAI-owned gateways.

code-execution.note: Setting allow_code_execution gives an agent an internal CodeInterpreterTool that runs generated Python and feeds errors back for retries.

human-in-loop.note: Tasks set human_input to pause a crew in a pending state; execution resumes through an endpoint taking the execution, task, feedback, and approval decision.

multi-tenancy.note: Only the commercial AMP platform provides an organization boundary with feature-level roles and entity-level permissions; the open-source library has no tenant scoping primitive.

declarative-deployment.note: YAML agent and task config declaratively defines one project, but there is no resource dependency graph, plan/apply cycle, or infrastructure provisioning.

agent-versioning.note: Updating a deployed crew rebuilds and redeploys from source with no immutable versions, aliases, staged rollout, or rollback.

skill-learning.note: The Memory class stores and retrieves scoped memories with recency and importance weighting, but does not synthesize reusable procedures from the agent's own trajectories.
